methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops targeting technology gap closure signal peer-driven capability building outside traditional tech hubs, testing whether grassroots distribution can counteract metro concentration dynamics.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership deepens institutional AI capability in the state capital but remains hub-anchored, creating a secondary excellence pocket that may not diffuse to surrounding regions without intentional distribution mechanisms.

signals.title: TAYLOR: AI data centers increase Virginia’s urban-rural divide - The Cavalier Daily
signals.signal_reading: Student op-ed explicitly naming data center concentration as driver of urban-rural divide signals awareness that infrastructure investment is deepening geographic inequality rather than distributing capability.

signals.title: Tony Stark’s J.A.R.V.I.S., meet Amelia, Norfolk Naval Shipyard’s IT AI help assistant - MilitaryNews.com
signals.signal_reading: Norfolk Naval Shipyard deploying AI assistant 'Amelia' represents platform-delivered adoption in defense sector—broad utility but shallow customization, diffusing access without building indigenous development capacity.

signals.title: University of Mary Washington Adds Virginia’s First Master’s Degree in AI in Business - Northern Virginia Magazine
signals.signal_reading: Virginia's first AI business master's degree at UMW concentrates advanced training in institutional settings, potentially creating credentialed excellence clusters while leaving non-degree pathways and rural learners underserved.
